Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# ast-grep(sg) ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting. ## What is ast-grep? ast-grep is an [abstract syntax tree](https://dev.to/balapriya/abstract-syntax-tree-ast-explained-in-plain-english-1h38) based tool to search code by pattern code. Think of it as your old-friend [`grep`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grep), but matching AST nodes instead of text. You can write patterns as if you are writing ordinary code. It will match all code that has the same syntactical structure. You can use `$` sign + upper case letters as a [wildcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildcard_character), e.g. `$MATCH`, to match any single AST node. Think of it as [regular expression dot](https://regexone.com/lesson/wildcards_dot) `.`, except it is not textual. Try the [online playground](https://ast-grep.github.io/playground.html) for a taste! ## Screenshot ![demo](https://ast-grep.github.io/image/search-replace.png) See more screenshots on the [website](https://ast-grep.github.io/). ## Installation You can install ast-grep from npm, pip, cargo, cargo-binstall, homebrew, scoop, mise, or MacPorts: ```bash npm install --global @ast-grep/cli # `pnpm approve-builds` may be needed pip install ast-grep-cli brew install ast-grep cargo install ast-grep --locked cargo binstall ast-grep # install via scoop scoop install main/ast-grep # install via MacPorts sudo port install ast-grep # try ast-grep in nix-shell nix-shell -p ast-grep # try ast-grep with mise mise use -g ast-grep ``` [Packages](https://repology.org/project/ast-grep/versions) are available on other platforms too. ## Command line usage ast-grep has the following form: ```bash ast-grep --pattern 'var code = $PATTERN' --rewrite 'let code = new $PATTERN' --lang ts ``` ### Examples * Rewrite code using null coalescing operator: ```bash ast-grep -p '$A && $A()' -l ts -r '$A?.()' ``` * Rewrite Zodios code: ```bash ast-grep -p 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF as const,)' -l ts -r 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF)' -i ``` ## Features ast-grep helps you search and replace code based on abstract syntax trees. It can help you do lightweight static analysis and massive scale code manipulation in an intuitive way. Key features: * **Intuitive pattern syntax**: Write patterns that look like ordinary code you would write every day (the pattern is isomorphic to code). * **jQuery-like API**: For AST traversal and manipulation. * **YAML configuration**: Write new linting rules or code modifications using YAML. * **Fast and scalable**: Utilizes multiple cores for performance. * **Beautiful CLI**: User-friendly command line interface. ## Use Cases * **Open-source library authors**: Help your library users adopt breaking changes more easily. * **Tech leads**: Enforce code best practices tailored to your business needs. * **Security researchers**: Write security rules much faster. ## More Information Visit the [official website](https://ast-grep.github.io/) for complete documentation and tutorials. ## Schemas JSON schemas for ast-grep rule configuration are available in the `schemas/` directory. """Behavioral regression tests, using only the new implementation."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EXECUTABLE = ROOT / 'executable'


class CliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def invoke(self, args, code='', cwd=None):
        return subprocess.run([str(EXECUTABLE), *args], input=code, text=True,
                              capture_output=True, cwd=cwd, timeout=10)

    def query(self, pattern, code, lang='js', extra=()):
        p = self.invoke(['-p', pattern, '-l', lang, '--stdin', '--json=compact', *extra], code)
        self.assertIn(p.returncode, (0, 1), p.stderr)
        return json.loads(p.stdout)

    def test_version_and_help(self):
        p = self.invoke(['--version'])
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'ast-grep 0.42.1\n')
        self.assertIn('AST pattern to match', self.invoke(['run', '--help']).stdout)

    def test_named_capture_and_range(self):
        values = self.query('console.log($A)', '  console.log(x);\n')
        self.assertEqual(len(values), 1)
        m = values[0]
        self.assertEqual(m['text'], 'console.log(x)')
        self.assertEqual(m['range']['byteOffset'], {'start': 2, 'end': 16})
        self.assertEqual(m['charCount'], {'leading': 2, 'trailing': 1})
        self.assertEqual(m['metaVariables']['single']['A']['text'], 'x')

    def test_repeated_variable(self):
        values = self.query('foo($A, $A)', 'foo(x,x); foo(x,y); foo(a + b, a+b);')
        self.assertEqual([v['text'] for v in values], ['foo(x,x)', 'foo(a + b, a+b)'])
        self.assertEqual(values[1]['metaVariables']['single']['A']['text'], 'a+b')

    def test_variadic_capture(self):
        values = self.query('foo($$$ARGS)', 'foo(); foo(a, b,);')
        self.assertEqual(values[0]['metaVariables']['multi']['ARGS'], [])
        self.assertEqual([n['text'] for n in values[1]['metaVariables']['multi']['ARGS']],
                         ['a', ',', 'b', ','])

    def test_python(self):
        values = self.query('print($$$ARGS)', 'print("hello", name)\nprint()\n', 'py')
        self.assertEqual(len(values), 2)
        self.assertEqual(values[0]['language'], 'Python')
        values = self.query('not $A', 'flag = not x == y', 'py')
        self.assertEqual(values[0]['metaVariables']['single']['A']['text'], 'x == y')

    def test_rewrite_stdin(self):
        p = self.invoke(['-p', 'foo($A)', '-r', 'bar($A)', '-l', 'js', '--stdin', '-U'],
                        'foo(1);\n')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, 'bar(1);\n\n')
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr, 'Applied 1 changes\n')

    def test_rewrite_diff(self):
        p = self.invoke(['-p', 'foo($A)', '-r', 'bar($A)', '-l', 'js', '--stdin'], 'foo(1);')
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,
                         'STDIN\n@@ -0,1 +0,1 @@\n1  │-foo(1);\n  1│+bar(1);\n')

    def test_rule_relations_and_transforms(self):
        rule = {'id': 'r', 'language': 'js', 'rule': {
            'pattern': 'foo($A)', 'inside': {'kind': 'function_declaration', 'stopBy': 'end'}},
            'transform': {'B': {'convert': {'source': '$A', 'toCase': 'snakeCase'}}},
            'fix': 'bar($B)', 'message': 'Use $B'}
        p = self.invoke(['scan', '--inline-rules', json.dumps(rule), '--stdin', '--json=compact'],
                        'foo(top); function f() { foo(myName); }')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
        values = json.loads(p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(len(values), 1)
        self.assertEqual(values[0]['replacement'], 'bar(my_name)')
        self.assertEqual(values[0]['message'], 'Use my_name')
        self.assertEqual(values[0]['labels'][1]['style'], 'secondary')

    def test_rule_error_exit(self):
        rule = 'id: r\nlanguage: js\nseverity: error\nrule:\n  pattern: foo($A)\n'
        p = self.invoke(['scan', '--inline-rules', rule, '--stdin', '--json=compact'], 'foo(x)')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn('1 error(s) found in code.', p.stderr)
        p = self.invoke(['scan', '--inline-rules', '{}', '--stdin'])
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 8)
        self.assertIn('missing field `language`', p.stderr)

    def test_language_injection(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            Path(d, 'page.html').write_text('<script>console.log(1)</script>\n')
            p = self.invoke(['-p', 'console.log($A)', '-l', 'js', '--json=compact'], cwd=d)
            values = json.loads(p.stdout)
            self.assertEqual(len(values), 1)
            self.assertEqual(values[0]['range']['byteOffset'], {'start': 8, 'end': 22})
            self.assertEqual(values[0]['language'], 'JavaScript')

    def test_project_and_tests(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = self.invoke(['new', 'project', '-y'], cwd=d)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
            p = self.invoke(['new', 'rule', 'no-foo', '-l', 'js', '-y'], cwd=d)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
            Path(d, 'rules', 'no-foo.yml').write_text(
                'id: no-foo\nlanguage: js\nrule:\n  pattern: foo($A)\nfix: bar($A)\n')
            Path(d, 'rule-tests', 'no-foo-test.yml').write_text(
                'id: no-foo\nvalid:\n- bar(1)\ninvalid:\n- foo(1)\n')
            p = self.invoke(['test', '--skip-snapshot-tests'], cwd=d)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
            self.assertIn('PASS no-foo  ..', p.stdout)
            p = self.invoke(['test', '-U'], cwd=d)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
            p = self.invoke(['test'], cwd=d)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr)
            self.assertIn('PASS no-foo  ..', p.stdout)

    def test_noisy_and_missing_tests(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            Path(d, 'rules').mkdir()
            Path(d, 'cases').mkdir()
            Path(d, 'sgconfig.yml').write_text('ruleDirs: [rules]\ntestConfigs:\n- testDir: cases\n')
            Path(d, 'rules', 'r.yml').write_text('id: r\nlanguage: js\nrule: {pattern: foo($A)}\n')
            Path(d, 'cases', 'r.yml').write_text('id: r\nvalid: ["foo(x)"]\ninvalid: ["bar(x)"]\n')
            p = self.invoke(['test', '--skip-snapshot-tests'], cwd=d)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 4)
            self.assertIn('FAIL r  NM', p.stdout)
            self.assertIn('ast-grep playground', p.stderr)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
